plot: At sunset in the garden Max wants to catch the moon and ask where it goes every morning; Dog thinks the moon is a giant ball to fetch, Max climbs on Dog who sits down, and Bird flies in dizzy circles, until Grandma explains that our world turns, not the moon, and shows them the moon that was rising over the tree the whole time.

script.title: Where Does the Moon Go in the Morning?

beats.say: Max! Max! Catch me! I flew too high, and now everything is spinning!
Whoa! Bird, you are going round and round like a spinning top!
It is sunset in the garden. The sky is pink and orange, and the flowers are closing.
Bird, why were you flying so high up there?
You asked me to look for the moon! You said it hides every single morning.
Yes! Every night the moon is up there, and every morning, poof, it is gone.
Tonight I will catch the moon, and I will ask it where it goes.
But I flew up, up, up, and I could not find it anywhere.
Max looks at the sky. There is the sun, going down slowly. But no moon yet.
Did somebody say ball? I heard a ball. I always hear balls.
Not a ball, Dog. The moon. The big round light in the night sky.
Big and round? That is a ball, Max. The biggest ball in the whole world!
When it comes up, I will jump really high and fetch it for you.
Okay! Plan number one. Dog fetches the moon.
They wait. And wait. Dog wags his tail so fast that he falls over.
Is it here yet? My tail is tired of waiting.
Not yet. Bird, can you fly up again? But just a little bit this time.
Just a little bit. I can do a little bit!
Bird flies to the top of a tall tree and looks all around the garden.
I see the house. I see the flowers. I see a worm. No moon!
Hmm. Maybe the moon is shy, like a kitten hiding under the bed.
Plan number two. I climb on Dog, and I look higher than everybody.
Climb on me? Okay. But no tickling, please.
Max climbs onto Dog's back. Dog giggles. Dog wiggles. Then Dog sits down.
Dog! You sat down! Now I am lower than before!
Sorry. Sitting is my favorite thing, after balls.
Your plans are very funny, Max. But the moon is still not here.
Then plan number three! We all shout very loud. Moon, come out!
Max shouts. Dog barks. Bird sings. The flowers shake. But the sky stays quiet.
Goodness me! Why is my garden so noisy at sunset?
Grandma, we want to catch the moon. Where does it go in the morning?
Oh, Max. The moon does not run away. And it does not hide in a box.
Our big world is round like a ball, and it turns very, very slowly.
When our side turns away, the moon goes out of sight for a while.
So the moon stays where it is, and we are the ones who move?
That's right. And here is a secret. Sometimes the moon stays in the morning sky too.
In the morning? With the sun? Two big balls at the same time?
Look up, my dears. Look just over the tall tree.
There it is. A soft, round moon, high above the garden, glowing like a lamp.
It was coming up the whole time, while we were busy shouting!
I flew right past it! I was looking the wrong way.
It is much too high to fetch. I will just say hello. Hello, big ball!
Moon, I wanted to catch you. But I think you look perfect right up there.
Some things are best for looking at, not for catching.
So Max does not catch the moon. He watches it with his friends, until the first stars come out.
Today I learned that waiting quietly shows you more than shouting.
And flying in circles makes you dizzy. I learned that too!
Now, who would like some warm milk before bed?
Me! Me! Is the milk shaped like a ball?
Everyone laughs, and the moon shines down on the sleepy garden.
And early tomorrow morning, I will look up and find the moon in the blue sky!
